text:
Day 4: Understanding the Stock Market 📈

The stock market can sound complicated, but at its core, it’s simply a marketplace where people buy and sell pieces of companies.

When you buy a stock, you’re buying a small ownership stake in a business. The price moves based on what investors think that business is worth and what they expect from it in the future.

That’s why prices can go up, down, and sometimes move for reasons that have nothing to do with what you expected.

Understanding how the market actually works is one of the first steps to becoming a better investor.

text:
Day 4: Understanding the Stock Market 📈

The stock market can sound complicated, but at its core, it’s simply a marketplace where people buy and sell pieces of companies.

When you buy a stock, you’re buying a small ownership stake in a business. The price moves based on what investors think that business is worth and what they expect from it in the future.

That’s why prices can go up, down, and sometimes move for reasons that have nothing to do with what you expected.

Understanding how the market actually works is one of the first steps to becoming a better investor.

text:
How to read the stock market

A big rally for stocks that began in Asia on Thursday lost steam after sweeping into Europe and the United States amid uncertainty about what will happen next after a U.S. court blocked many of President Donald Trump’s sweeping tariffs .

The S&P 500 rose 0.4% after giving up more than half of an early gain. The Dow Jones Industrial Average added 117 points, or 0.3%, and the Nasdaq composite rose 0.4%.
It’s a downshift after stocks initially leaped nearly 2% in Tokyo and Seoul, where markets had the first chance to react to the ruling late Wednesday by the U.S. Court of International Trade. 

The court said that the 1977 International Emergency Economic Powers Act that Trump cited for ordering massive increases in taxes on imports from around the world does not authorize the use of tariffs.

text:
Trump Calls Bitcoin “Very Powerful” at Fintech Event

President Donald Trump spoke positively about Bitcoin at a fintech event on Friday, calling it “very powerful” and noting that more people are choosing to use crypto for payments.

His comments reflect a noticeable shift toward supporting the crypto industry during his second term. The administration has been engaging with major crypto companies like Coinbase and has pushed back against banks over delays in crypto-related regulations, including stablecoin rules.

At the time of his remarks, Bitcoin was trading between roughly $66,000 and $69,000, showing some volatility after recently nearing the $70,000 mark.

Trump’s stance is part of a broader effort to position the U.S. as a more crypto-friendly environment. Online reactions were mixed, with some users feeling bullish while others joked about prices dipping right after his comments.
